assertion_analysis.fails_if: The pane draws the sentence more than once, draws anything else beside it (an unknown-run row), or prints nothing; restoring the removed producer-slow list entry reddens it, as negative-control.log line 60 records.
The text branch ignores pane_line and prints the sentence; negative-control.log line 73 records it failing with the unknown-run row.
The follower emits zero or more than one JSON object for the event; this is the JSON case's one independent expectation besides the literal at :387.

The emitted object drops or renames one of the carried keys; it is an echo assertion - the expected side is event[field], the dict the test itself handed in - so it holds for any code that re-emits that dict.
The emitted run_id is not the null the test supplied; same echo shape as :396.

assertion_independence: Two added assertions compare a value against the same input the test handed in: :361-363 compares the pane's text against SLOW_SENTENCE, the very string carried as event["line"], and :396-397 compares the emitted fields against event[field]. The first is still a guard for this defect because the exclusivity half (nothing else on the pane) reddens on the mutation, as negative-control.log shows; the second is not, and the log records the JSON case passing under that mutation.

0.reason: the JSON case guards only a dropped key; the text and pane_line cases carry the regression, and a stronger JSON case is not worth another round

1.reason: the follower fix landed from a peer with its own test before this run launched; the duplicated harness is test-only and costs nothing at runtime

findings.summary: The JSON case cannot fail on the regression it was added for: negative-control.log records it as the single pass while the text and pane_line cases fail, because an unlisted producer-slow still reaches _emit_crew_result on the fall-through path at reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:3810, and its per-field loop at :396 compares the emitted object against the very dict the test handed in, so the case only detects a dropped key. The JSON arm therefore adds no guard the sibling file does not already carry.

_follow_one re-implements the follower-render harness already written inline at tests/test_a_producer_loss_reaches_the_pane.py:174-180 (patch _follow_watch_lines and _hand_off_from_follower, then CliRunner().invoke(follow.crew, ["follow", ..."--no-color"] + ["--json"])); the three cases also duplicate coverage that file held at the base revision, where :159-186 asserts a producer-slow notice prints its line and draws no unknown row in both text and JSON modes and :266-292 already asserts the pane_line=False silence. A defect in either place can now regress in the other unnoticed.
